description: Ω12 — reprogrammability as DATA, never codegen (D-219). Rules are vault objects (ns 'automation'), teachings are vault objects (ns 'nlcl'), the fired ledger is a vault object per processed message; a deterministic 500ms tick loop scans vault ns 'email' for new/unseen inbox revisions, matches rules by the shared contact derivation, and executes actions THROUGH THE PORT under principal vivim.director — the law still gates every rule action (one consent at rule-creation time, granted by the user through the console). Swapping this plugin swaps the automation engine; the rules and teachings survive in the vault.

engine.doc: rule {when:{event:'message.received', from:'contact:<slug>'|null}, then:{op, payload}} → vault.append@1 (ns automation, id rule:<from-slug|any>-forward[-n]) → {ruleId, rev, summary, actionConsent:{principal:'vivim.director', op}}. Engines declare no risk; semantics are READ/derivative — the op itself only appends a vault data object; the rule's ACTION op executes later, through the port, under principal vivim.director, gated by law.check. v1 vocabulary boundaries (fail-closed): when.event MUST be 'message.received'; then.op MUST be 'message.send@1' (the only action op the director executes); then.payload must be an object; then.payload.messageFromTrigger===true binds the trigger message (body=trigger body, subject=then.payload.subject ?? 'Fwd: <subject>'). actionConsent lets the surface pre-check law.check so the console grants ONCE at rule-creation time.

registry {filter:'rules'} → {rules:[{id, enabled, summary, when, then, createdAt}]} (vault.query ns automation idPrefix 'rule:' + bounded gets). registry {action:'enable'|'disable', ruleId} → vault.get + a new revision with enabled flipped → the updated rule (append-only disable/enable — revertable by construction). READ/derivative: both forms only read/append vault data; unknown ruleId → DEGRADED.

teach {word, op, action?:'add'|'remove'} → vault.append@1 (ns nlcl, id lexicon:<folded word>) with data.op = op (add) or null (remove). op:null IS the removal mechanism — the mind skips op:null rows, so 'unteach' is an append, never a delete. READ/derivative: a data revision only; future parses change because the WorldModel carries the lexicon. Validation (fail-closed): word folds to ^[a-z0-9-]{2,20}$; op matches <id>@<version> when action is add.

tick {} → {scanned, processed, fired:[{messageId, ruleId, ok, error?, consentId?}]} — the deterministic fire pass (also scheduled live: setInterval 500ms, config.intervalMs, in-flight guard, cleared on shutdown). Scans vault ns 'email' (bounded 200 rows) for new/changed revisions, fetches EVERY unresolved candidate in ONE vault.getmany@1 hop and checks the fired ledger for every trigger candidate in ONE more (D-388 — the read phase costs 2 batched hops regardless of candidate count), keeps inbox+unseen+non-self messages, skips messages already in the fired ledger, matches enabled rules (sorted by id asc, loaded lazily per-row) via contactFromAddress (the shared derivation, D-216), fires each action through port:message.send@1 under principal vivim.director — law-gated; a REFUSED/consent-required result is a LEGITIMATE ledgered outcome (the user grants through the console; the next trigger fires clean — no retry spin). One ledger append per processed message after all rules attempted. Never throws: per-rule errors and vault failures are captured into the result/ledger (partial report).

classify {op?, archetypeSlug?, event?, from?} → {decisionId, kind, capability, branch, reason, rev} — D-323 computation-kind routing: enabled automation rule → DETERMINISTIC + its op; else PROMOTED providers realization → class-mapped kind (SIMULATOR→DETERMINISTIC, else PROBABILISTIC) + '<slug>@1'; else HUMAN + empty capability (escalate). Contradictory op/slug refused fail-closed. Appends decision rev 1 to vault ns 'resolve' (id resolve:<decisionId>, buildDecisionRef D-323). READ/derivative: data revision only; never touches the hot run.submit path.

report {decisionId, status:'ok'|'failed', execMs} → {decisionId, rev, status} — appends outcome rev 2 to the SAME ns 'resolve' object (two revs of one object: decision then outcome). UNKNOWN when the decision doesn't exist (expected-but-negative, never a throw). READ/derivative: data revision only.

scorecard {} → {rows:[{kind, capability, n, okRate, p50ExecMs}], at} — pure aggregation over ns 'resolve' grouped (kind, capability); p50 is the lower median. No thresholds, no auto-actions: scoreboards inform, they never decide. READ/derivative: reads only.

capabilities.justification: Rules, teachings, and the fired ledger are VAULT OBJECTS — data/code divorce: the director owns no storage, so persisting/appending them needs port:vault.append@1, and scanning email state + loading rules/ledger needs port:vault.query@1 and port:vault.get@1. The tick's read phase is batched (D-388): every unresolved candidate's body and the whole fired-ledger check ride ONE vault.getmany@1 hop each instead of up to 2×200 sequential vault.get@1 round trips per tick. Rule ACTIONS execute through port:message.send@1 under principal vivim.director so the LAW still gates them — one consent at rule-creation time, granted by the user through the console. The composition grants exactly these five per user-signed Recipe — never this manifest.
